messages:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER DUTY ALERT - SERVING-RUNTIME_HIGH - nccl_collective_timeouts detected on inference-gpu-pool-7 (auto-triggered paging)

mira: noticed spiking 5xxs and a couple of node reboots in the last 8m, most traffic to model 'llama-44b-tp' tensor-parallel variant. seeing repeated NCCL timeouts in runtime logs. paging oncall-sre.

sanjay: logs (tail from one affected pod):
```
2026-01-28 10:12:34.512 INFO runtime: starting inference loop
2026-01-28 10:12:35.641 ERROR runtime: NCCL WARN Timeout, rank 1, ncclComm 0x7f8b9e...
2026-01-28 10:12:35.642 ERROR runtime: CUDA: unhandled error: CUBLAS_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR
2026-01-28 10:12:36.010 CRITICAL runtime: pod terminating due to OOM-kill / GPU reset
```

julia: infra events show flapping on node gpu-07: kubelet reports "container runtime is restarting", dmesg shows GPU reset and nvlink errors. initial suspicion: interconnect (NVLink) flaps causing NCCL communicators to hang -> runtime stuck -> watchdog OOM / pod crash.

infra-bot: kubectl events snippet:
```
Type    Reason     Age    From               Message
----    ------     ---    ----               -------
Warning Unhealthy 6m     kubelet, gpu-07    Liveness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 500
Warning BackOff   5m     kubelet, gpu-07    Back-off restarting failed container
Normal  Killing   5m     kubelet, gpu-07    Container runtime triggered SIGKILL
```

henry: quick mitigation plan: 1) isolate node, 2) restart runtime on affected pods, 3) failover traffic to single-GPU variant for the model while we triage, 4) collect NCCL + NVML logs + core dumps.

mira: running the commands now to gather data. pasting steps so oncall can pick up if I get pulled: 
```sh
# get affected pods
kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=llama-44b-tp
# describe one
kubectl -n inference describe pod llama-44b-tp-ff7k
# container logs (runtime container)
kubectl -n inference logs llama-44b-tp-ff7k -c runtime --tail=500
# check node GPU state
ssh gpu-07 sudo nvidia-smi -q -d ERROR,UTILIZATION,POWER
# dump dmesg lines related to NV and GPU
ssh gpu-07 sudo dmesg | egrep -i "nvrm|nvlink|gpu" | tail -n 200
```

sanjay: enabling extra debug for the running launchers to capture NCCL/debug traces and forcing a collector for core files: set env NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=ALL RD_KILL_ON_ERROR=1 and restart container. Also set "--gcore-on-crash" in runtime config to preserve coredump.

julia: suggestion for live mitigation that doesn't require code changes: roll routing rule to model variant 'llama-44b-gpu-single' (same weights but no tensor parallelism) and bump concurrency limits down to avoid packing many KVs into one communicator. That will remove multi-GPU collectives until we finish root cause.

mira: applying interim route change: 
```json
{
  "route": "/v1/generate/llama-44b",
  "model_priority": ["llama-44b-gpu-single", "llama-44b-quantized"],
  "max_concurrency": 4
}
```
applied with the console routing API. Observing tail: 503s dropping from 18% -> 6% in 4m. Customers with high QPS may still see latency increase.

henry: collecting NVML and NCCL logs — please capture /var/log/nvidia-installer.log and the runtime's nccl trace. commands: 
```sh
sudo journalctl -u runtime -o short-iso --since "10 minutes ago" | egrep -i "nccl|cuda|cublas|nvrm" > /tmp/runtime-nccl.log
sudo cp /var/log/nvidia* /tmp/ ; sudo chown $USER:$USER /tmp/*nvidia*
# if core available
sudo coredumpctl dump --output=/tmp/runtime.core --no-guess
```

infra-bot: node gpu-07 cordoned and drained: `kubectl cordon gpu-07 && kubectl drain gpu-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data` :white_check_mark:

mira: restarted 3 affected pods onto gpu-12 and gpu-13 (different rack), waiting for warm KV cache to prime. temp autoscale +2 replicas for the pool to absorb traffic while single-gpu route ramps.

sanjay: added a temporary runtime guard to detect stuck NCCL communicators and trigger graceful fallback to single-GPU variant for this model after 10s collective stall. patch applied to runtime-config and rolling restart scheduled.

oncall-sre: taking over at 10:32 UTC for the rest of the incident. summary for handoff: 
- Impact: intermittent 5xxs and increased latency for llama-44b customers using tensor-parallel variant. Roughly ~12% of requests 5xx at peak, now reduced to ~4% after route fallback. No customer data exposure.
- Root cause (working hypothesis): multi-GPU NCCL communicators timed out due to NVLink/interconnect flaps on gpu-07; communicator hang cascaded to OOMs and container restarts.
- Actions taken: cordoned gpu-07; collected runtime & dmesg logs; enabled NCCL debug; routed traffic to single-GPU variant; scaled pool +2; applied runtime guard to fallback on communicator stall; collecting cores & nvml logs for postmortem.
- Next steps: SRE to own node hardware validation (firmware/NVLink cable checks), infra to correlate system-level metrics across the rack, runtime team to evaluate communicator watchdog behavior and consider soft timeouts + retry logic in the serving runtime.

oncall-sre: assigning followups: @henry to coordinate hardware ticket (fw update / nvlink reseat); @sanjay to file PR for communicator watchdog tests; @julia to include this incident in weekly infra sync and confirm whether adjacent nodes saw NIC/NVLink errors.

julia: creating a short incident ticket in postmortems with initial timeline and attaching logs: postmortems/2026-01-28-nccl-stall-llama44b-draft.md :eyes:

mira: thumbs up, continuing to monitor for 30m then will close paging if stable. :thumbsup: (2)

henry: one more note for followup — capture the exact NCCL version and driver: `nvidia-smi -q | grep -i "Driver Version" && python -c 'import cupy; print(cupy.__version__)'` and verify on gpu-07 vs gpu-12.

oncall-sre: handing off to next on-call at 11:00 UTC — please pick up the ticket and the file in postmortems. If anything spikes, re-open PAGER. thanks all for quick response. :pray:

pagerduty-bot: incident auto-ack cleared (condition recovered)
